newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Brady bond oil warrants ready for a payout.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Brady bond oil warrants ready for a payout.

text.p: The oil warrants embedded in the Mexico Brady bonds are in the money for a payment on March 31, and stand a good chance to pay out for the rest of the year, ING Barings said in a report on Monday.
The March payment would be the second after a similar one tied to the Oil Value Recovery Rights (VRRs) made at the end of December last year, ING Barings quantitative analyst Anna Titarchuk said.
"We see them in the money for March 31. It will be the second payment after the payment they made at the end of December," Titarchuk told Reuters.
The payments are tied to the price of crude oil over the previous four quarters. That oil price has been higher than forecast.

"You have very high prices at the end of last year, and and we know the approximate price for the first quarter of 1997 and even if the prices declines somewhat in the second quarter, you will still have a payment above zero," she said.
The payment amounts on the VRRs are seen peaking by June 1997, or perhaps sooner, and if world crude prices remain stable or decline, to then to decrease over the course of this year.

The commonly-quoted yield spreads exclude VRR value due to the lack of liquidity of these oil warrants, "thus, despite the recent decline in world crude prices, Mexico Bradys still remain cheap relative to other assets in the market on a spread basis," she said.
ING Barings estimates the payment on March 31 will be 15.65 cents for $100.00 of face value of the Par bonds, and 24.08 cents for each $100.00 of Discount bonds.
